items.text: Gary Pilnick, the CEO of Kellogg’s, suggested families facing financial strain could consider having cereal for dinner as a more affordable option. He emphasized the affordability of cereal compared to other meal choices and highlighted the company’s marketing efforts to promote this idea. When questioned about the potential backlash , Pilnick expressed confidence in the concept’s reception , citing its growing popularity as a trend. He explained that cereal consumption extends beyond breakfast, with a significant portion consumed at dinner or as a snack. Pilnick’s remarks reflect the company’s strategy to adapt to consumer needs amid financial pressures. However, his suggestion sparked debate over the appropriateness of such advice for families experiencing economic hardship. Difficult words: strain (pressure or tension), backlash (a strong negative reaction to something), reception (how something is received or accepted). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Gary Pilnick is the CEO of Kellogg’s, a company which makes cereals. Recently, he said that families which have money problems should consider having cereal for dinner as a cheaper option . Pilnick said this during an interview, and he explained that cereal is more affordable than other foods. The company wants to promote this idea through advertising. When reporters asked him if this idea could cause problems, Pilnick said that cereal was becoming more popular. He explained that many people eat cereal not just for breakfast but also for dinner or as a snack. Pilnick’s comments show how Kellogg’s is trying to help people save money during difficult times. Difficult words: option (one thing which you can choose), affordable (not expensive), promote (to support something or help something become successful). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Kellogs is a company which makes cereals . Many people eat cereal for dinner. The boss of Kellogg’s says that families can eat cereal for dinner, too. It is cheaper than other foods. He thinks that it is a good idea. Many people already eat cereal for dinner or as a snack. The company is trying to help people save money. Eating cereal instead of other food may be a good idea. This is what the boss of Kellogg’s thinks. Kellogg’s wants to put a lot of money into advertising cereal for dinner. Some people do not like this idea. Cereals have a lot of sugar in them. Eating cereals in the evening is not healthy . Difficult words: cereals (roasted grain which people often eat with milk for breakfast), advertising (ways how to make people know a product, usually on TV or the internet), healthy (good for your body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Alabama’s Supreme Court ruling that frozen embryos are children has sparked division among Christian groups. While the decision didn’t directly prohibit IVF , it has caused uncertainty and fear of legal consequences. Margaret Boyce, a devout Christian, feels the ruling adds unnecessary anxiety to an already challenging IVF process. Chief Justice’s biblical justification of the ruling has led to mixed reactions, with some anti-abortion groups praising it as pro-life. The ruling extends existing laws on wrongful death to include embryos in storage facilities, further complicating the situation for fertility clinics. Local lawmakers are under pressure to find a solution, with Republicans planning to introduce a bill to protect IVF. However, the issue remains contentious , with Democrats sensing both opportunity and danger. The ruling has ignited a new battle over reproductive rights in Alabama. Difficult words: IVF (a process of fertilization where a woman’s egg is combined with a man’s sperm in a laboratory dish), biblical (relating to or contained in the Bible), contentious (controversial). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Alabama’s top court said that frozen embryos are children. This caused a fight among Christian groups. The court didn’t ban IVF , but many people worry about the legal impact of the decision. Many clinics stopped treatments. Margaret is a Christian she finds the news worrying. On the other hand, some groups which support life, are happy about the decision. The ruling also changed laws on embryos which clinics keep in storage . Local lawmakers plan to introduce a bill to protect IVF which could help solve the problem. The ruling started a new fight over the rights of unborn children in Alabama. Difficult words: embryo (an early stage of a baby or other animal before birth), IVF (putting a man’s sperm into a woman’s egg outside the woman’s body), storage (storing something for future use). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A court in Alabama, US, says that frozen embryos are children. This causes fights among Christians. IVF is a method by which a specialist puts a man’s sperm into a woman’s egg. This happens in a lab, outside the woman’s body. Fertilization clinics now stop doing this. Some Christians are unhappy about the court’s ruling . But some groups like it. They say that people must protect embryos, too. Politicians must solve the problem quickly. Some politicians worry. In Alabama, the fight over IVF is big. It has an impact on the lives of many people. Difficult words: embryo (a very early stage of a baby or other animal inside the mother’s body), fertilization clinic (a place where specialists help couples have a baby), ruling (when a court decides something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Germany recently joined a select group of nations legalizing cannabis, allowing individuals and voluntary associations to cultivate and possess limited amounts of the drug. The law permits growing up to three plants for personal use and owning up to 25 grams of cannabis. Additionally, non-commercial cannabis production is sanctioned for cannabis clubs with a maximum of 500 adult members. The government aims to combat the black market and enhance youth protection with this move. Health Minister Karl Lauterbach defended the law, citing the need to address rising cannabis use among young people and the increasing potency of street drugs. Despite criticism from the opposition, the law aims to regulate cannabis use while maintaining restrictions on its consumption near schools and playgrounds. Difficult words: cultivate (to prepare the land and grow something on it), sanctioned (permitted), potency (the power or strength). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Germany recently legalized cannabis. This allowed people and groups to grow their plants and keep limited amounts of cannabis. People can grow up to three plants and possess up to 25 grams. Cannabis clubs with fewer than 500 members can also produce cannabis. The goal is to reduce the black market and protect young people. Health Minister Karl Lauterbach defends the law, he says that more young people are using cannabis nowadays. Other people argue that legalizing cannabis will not stop drug dealing. Difficult words: legalize (to make something legal), possess (to keep), defend (to support something what many people don’t like). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Germany has a new law . It is okay now to have and grow a little bit of cannabis . People can grow three plants and have 25 grams. The government wants to stop the black market and keep children safe. The Health Minister says that more young people are using cannabis. Street drugs are stronger now. But some people do not think that this new law will stop drug selling. Difficult words: law (an official rule), cannabis (a tall plant which some people use as a drug), black market (business activities which are against the rules of a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

South Korean trainee doctors are on strike protesting against the government’s plan to increase medical school admissions . The strike involves nearly 8,000 trainees who argue that pay and working conditions need improvement before admitting more students. Their absence affects hospitals, leading to canceled surgeries and overwhelmed emergency rooms. Trainee doctors work long hours, up to 100 hours a week, and believe hiring more senior staff is a solution. They also fear increased competition with more medical students. The government aims to address a future doctor shortage by increasing admissions by 2,000 students by 2025. However, critics argue that existing doctors are sufficient, and increasing admissions won’t address underlying issues of pay and overwork. The strike intensifies as the government issues back-to-work orders and promises legal action against non-compliant doctors. Difficult words: admission (the process of accepting someone into an institution), underlying (basic), non-compliant (not doing what someone asks you to do). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Trainee doctors in South Korea are protesting against the government’s plan to accept more students to medical schools. Doctors argue that improving pay and working conditions is more important than admitting more students. The protests disrupt hospital services, hospitals cancel surgeries, and emergency rooms and full. Trainees work long hours and they believe that hiring senior staff would solve the problems. The government plans to admit 2,000 students by 2025 to deal with future doctor shortages . Some people say that there are enough doctors, and the plan will not solve more important problems. Difficult words: disrupt (to bring problems or difficulties), senior staff (people who do a job for a longer time and have more skills), shortage (not enough of something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

South Korean trainee doctors are protesting. They do not want more students in medical schools. Doctors want better pay and less work. The protest stops hospital work. Hospitals must cancel surgeries . The government wants more students to become doctors. There may not be enough doctors in the future. But current doctors say that there are enough already. They want better money first. The government tells doctors to go back to work. If not, they may have problems. But the fight may continue for a long time. Difficult words: trainee (a person who is learning something new), surgery (a procedure to fix a person’s body), continue (to not stop). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Israel has threatened to withdraw from the Eurovision Song Contest if organizers attempt to censor its entry. This threat comes amidst controversy over whether Israel’s entry, sung by Eden Golan, violates rules on political neutrality. Golan’s song ‘October Rain’ allegedly references the Gaza conflict. Israel insists it won’t participate if the song faces censorship. The disputed lyrics include phrases like ‘Boys Don’t Cry’ and ‘Flowers’ which are military slang for war fatalities. Eurovision organizers, known as the EBU, are scrutinizing the song’s political content. They emphasize the contest’s apolitical stance but acknowledge the need to uphold rules against political messaging. The situation mirrors past instances where countries faced disqualification for political song content. With a deadline looming, Israel’s stance remains firm, signaling a potential showdown over artistic expression versus contest regulations. Difficult words: scrutinize (to examine closely), apolitical stance (when someone isn’t interested or connected with politics), showdown (an important argument that’s intended to end an existing disagreement). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Israel threatened to leave Eurovision if organizers censored its entry. The song ‘October Rain’ by Eden Golan reportedly refers to the Gaza conflict. Eurovision rules prohibit political messages in songs. Eurovision’s organizer, the EBU, is currently checking the song’s lyrics. The lyrics include things like ‘Boys Don’t Cry’ and ‘Flowers’ which is a word that soldiers use when they speak about killed people. Similar incidents already happened in the past and countries faced disqualification for political lyrics. Israel keeps saying that the song is okay and there is no reason for disqualification. Difficult words: censor (to check if books, films, or songs do not include political or dangerous things), prohibit (to not allow something), disqualification (when someone must leave a competition because he or she doesn’t follow rules). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Israel may leave Eurovision. There is a problem with its song. Eden Golan sings the song called ‘October Rain’. Some people believe that the song is about the Gaza conflict . Eurovision has strict rules . The rules say no politics in songs. Eurovision is checking the song. There are things like ‘Boys Don’t Cry’ or ‘Flowers’ in the song. Soldiers sometimes use the word ‘flowers’ when they speak about dead people. Other countries get in trouble for political songs before. Singers want to use Eurovision for political messages. It is not a new thing. But Israel says that the song is okay. Difficult words: conflict (a fight), rule (a thing you must or must not do). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

European countries bought significant quantities of the antiviral medication Paxlovid to combat COVID-19; however, a substantial portion is at risk of expiring, amounting to around 3.1 million unused courses across the UK, Germany, Spain, Italy, and France. Despite its effectiveness in reducing severe illness by nearly 90%, Paxlovid faces underutilization due to declining infection rates and high vaccination coverage, leading to reduced demand. Challenges in prescribing criteria , distribution efficiency, and risk assessment contribute to its limited use. Furthermore, the drug’s complex nature, consisting of two components with potential drug interactions, poses difficulties for physicians, particularly in older patients. While some countries like France have simplified access to Paxlovid, ensuring effective use remains a challenge, highlighting the complexities of balancing risk and benefit in healthcare decision-making. Difficult words: underutilization (the state of not being used to the fullest content), criterion (a principle or standard by which something may be judged or decided), complexity (when something is difficult or complicated). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

European countries quickly bought Paxlovid, an antiviral drug which is effective against COVID-19. But now, millions of unused courses are expiring soon. The drug reduces severe illness risk by nearly 90%, which is why many countries were interested in it. But the demand decreased. Many people already got a vaccine and there are not so many new cases. Moreover, the drug has two components , which means more challenges for doctors. The drug may interact with other drugs, especially in older patients. Europe may waste around 3.1 million unused courses worth billions of euros. Difficult words: antiviral (a drug which people use to cure an infection a virus causes), demand (when many people want something), component (one or more parts). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Europe buys lots of COVID-19 medicine Paxlovid. This is when there are many sick people. But now, many medicines may go bad. The medicine helps with bad COVID. But doctors do not use it much anymore. It is hard for doctors to give it to people. The medicine has two parts. It can be tricky . Some people have problems with it. It is better to take it early in COVID. But many people do not know when to take it. Europe has now around 3.1 million courses . The price of them is billions of euros. And nobody may use the drug. Some countries will throw it away. Difficult words: tricky (difficult), course (one single piece of medicine which a doctor uses). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An international police operation, dubbed Operation Kronos, successfully dismantled the LockBit ransomware group, notorious for its malicious activities. Fourteen countries collaborated in the operation, leading to the closure of 34 servers primarily located in the Netherlands, Germany, Finland, France, Switzerland, Australia, the US, and the UK. Additionally, two individuals associated with the group were arrested in Poland and Ukraine. Over 200 cryptocurrency accounts linked to the criminal enterprise were frozen. LockBit has inflicted substantial damage on thousands of victims worldwide, targeting various organizations, including government agencies, hospitals, schools, and high-profile companies. The group executed over 1,700 attacks globally. Experts hail the operation as the most significant ransomware disruption to date, underscoring its crucial role in combating cybercrime. Difficult words: notorious (famous or well known, typically for some bad quality), inflict (to cause something unpleasant or painful), underscore (to emphasize the importance of something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

An international police operation named Operation Kronos shut down a hacker group. The LockBit ransomware group is well known for its harmful actions. Fourteen countries got together and they closed 34 servers across various locations, including the Netherlands, Germany, Finland, France, Switzerland, Australia, the US, and the UK. Police arrested two people linked to the group in Poland and Ukraine, and froze more than 200 cryptocurrency accounts. LockBit targeted government agencies, hospitals, schools, and global companies, and the group conducted over 1,700 attacks worldwide. Experts say that the operation was the most important disruption to ransomware ever. Difficult words: ransomware (bad software which steals information and then wants money for it), target (to choose someone or something and an object of attack), disruption (problems which interrupt an event or activity). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Police hurt a bad computer group called LockBit. It is a ransomware group. They steal information from computers. Then, they want money for the information. 14 countries work together. They find 34 computer places in Europe, Australia, and the US. Two people go to prison in Poland and Ukraine. Police stop more than 200 cryptocurrency accounts, too. LockBit hurt many people. They attack schools, government offices, and big companies. There are more than 1,700 attacks. Police say that it is a big win against hackers . Experts say that it is the biggest stop to hackers ever. Difficult words: steal (to take something what does not belong to you and keep it), cryptocurrency (digital money), hacker (a person who gets to other people’s computers and gets information from them). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The High Court in London has commenced proceedings regarding an appeal by Julian Assange, the founder of WikiLeaks, against his extradition to the US on espionage charges. Assange’s supporters argue that he’s facing persecution for releasing classified US documents that influenced diplomacy and public opinion. Assange’s legal team is seeking an appeal against the extradition order issued by the British Home Secretary in 2022. US prosecutors intend to try Assange for spying, though he was absent from the court due to illness. If extradited, Assange could face life imprisonment, sparking concerns among his supporters about his safety and the freedom of the press. His lawyers argue that the case is politically motivated and could set a dangerous precedent for journalists globally. Despite the possibility of an appeal to the European Court of Human Rights, the outcome remains uncertain, with fears that extradition could occur swiftly. Difficult words: extradition (the legal process of surrendering an individual to another country), classified (officially stated to be secret), try (to subject someone to trial). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The High Court in London is hearing an appeal by Julian Assange against his extradition to the US on espionage charges. Assange’s supporters say that the US wants him because he revealed secret US documents. His lawyers want to appeal against the extradition order by the British Home Secretary in 2022. Some people worry that if Assange ends up in the US, he may spend the rest of his life in prison. Assange’s lawyers believe that there is a lot of politics in his case, and they believe that it can hurt journalists and press freedom . If the appeal fails, Assange will have one last chance, to appeal to the European Court of Human Rights. Difficult words: extradition (when a country officially sends a person to another country to face a trial), appeal (to apply to a higher court to review a case), press freedom (when the government doesn’t control what journalists say or write). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The court in London is deciding whether Julian Assange should go to the US. Assange is in trouble. He shows secret US documents. This has an impact on politics and diplomacy . Assange is in London, but US officials want him in the US. If Assange returns to the US, he may go to prison for espionage . A court decides to send Assange to the US in 2022. Assange’s people want to change this. Maybe, another court can help. But it is not sure. People are afraid of what will happen to journalists if Assange goes away. They believe that it is not fair to journalists. The government must not tell journalists what to write or speak about. Difficult words: diplomacy (how countries speak with each other), espionage (doing things secretly to get information about countries or important people), journalist (a person who writes for newspapers, magazines, or news websites). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent visit to the UAE aimed to bolster ties and expand India’s influence, strategically timed ahead of impending elections. Despite historical tensions, Modi inaugurated Abu Dhabi’s first Hindu temple, symbolizing closer relations with the region. The temple is part of Modi’s Hindu-centric agenda and it signifies India’s growing presence in the UAE, home to over 3 million Indians. The visit also saw agreements on trade corridors and investments, signaling deepening economic cooperation. Modi’s efforts align with his bid for global leadership, as he positions himself favorably for the upcoming elections, leveraging his popularity among Hindu voters. Difficult words: impending (about to happen), agenda (a list of things to be considered or solved), leverage (to use to maximum advantage). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited the UAE to strengthen ties and show India’s influence. This trip happened just before India’s elections. Although there were troubles between the UAE and India in the past, Modi inaugurated Abu Dhabi’s first Hindu temple. The UAS is home to over 3 million Indians, and Modi is focusing on them now. The visit also led to agreements on trade and investments . The two countries are working together more than ever. Modi wants to boost his image as a global leader, and he needs Hindus to support him in the elections. Difficult words: inaugurate (to formally open or start), investment (putting money into a business or activity), boost (to help or encourage something to increase or improve). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

India’s Prime Minister Modi goes to the UAE for a visit. It happens before India’s elections . Modi opens a new Hindu temple in the UAE. It is important because it shows India’s strong connection with the UAE. The temple is big. Over 2 million Indians live in the UAE. Modi knows that he needs Hindus in the elections. Modi also makes deals with the UAE to do a lot of business together. This visit helps Modi look good before the elections because many Indians like him and his party . Difficult words: elections (when people vote to choose their leaders), temple (a building where people talk to a god), party (a group of people who have the same political ideas). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Greece has become the first Orthodox Christian nation to legalize same-sex marriage. Despite opposition from the Orthodox Church, the law change is seen as a significant advancement by supporters. Joyous celebrations erupted in Athens as crowds hailed the milestone moment for LGBTQ+ rights in Greek society. The legislation, which also strengthens parental rights for same-sex couples, marks a historic shift in the predominantly Orthodox Christian country. While critics argue there’s room for improvement, many view this move as a pivotal step towards equality. The decision garnered a rare cross-party consensus in Parliament, with both left-wing and conservative lawmakers supporting the motion. Greece’s stance on same-sex marriage may set a precedent for other Orthodox nations, although the church remains firm in its disapproval. Difficult words: predominantly (mainly, for the most part), pivotal (central and important), consensus (wide agreement). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Greece became the first Orthodox Christian country to allow same-sex marriage. Some people, like the Orthodox Church, don’t agree with this change. But many others were happy about it and celebrated in Athens. The new law also gives more rights to same-sex parents. Even though some people still think there is more to improve, many people see this decision as a big step towards fairness . In Greece’s Parliament, lawmakers from different political parties agreed on this change, which doesn’t usually happen. This decision may have an impact on other Orthodox countries, but it is not clear yet. Difficult words: right (what you can have or do), fairness (when you are fair), lawmaker (a politician). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Greece decides about something important. They say yes to same-sex marriage . Same-sex marriage means that two men or two women can marry. Greece is the first Orthodox Christian country which do this. The church does not like this idea. But others think that it is good and important. People in Greece celebrate in Athens. They feel happy because they wait for this for a long time. Now, same-sex couples can have the same rights as everyone else. It is a big change for Greece. Greece is a country where many people follow the Orthodox Church. Other countries may also decide to allow same-sex marriage. But we have to wait and see. Difficult words: marriage (when two people get married), orthodox (when someone has the same ideas and beliefs as many people), right (what you can have or do). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Russian opposition figure Alexei Navalny died in custody after collapsing during a walk at the ‘Polar Wolf’ Arctic penal colony, where he was serving a lengthy sentence. The death of Navalny, known for his anti-corruption activism, has drawn condemnation from Western leaders, who hold Russia accountable. Navalny’s demise leaves a significant void in the Russian opposition landscape as President Putin solidifies his grip on power. Western officials, including US President Biden, have denounced Russia’s role in Navalny’s death. Navalny’s sudden demise has sparked allegations of foul play , though authorities haven’t confirmed the cause of death. Despite Navalny’s passing, his legacy as a prominent critic of Putin’s regime endures, inspiring hope for change among some segments of Russian society. Difficult words: void (an empty space), solidify (make stronger), foul play (criminal or violent behavior that results in someone’s death). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Alexei Navalny, a big critic of Russian President Putin, died after collapsing during a walk at the Arctic prison. Western leaders, including US President Biden, criticized Russia for Navalny’s death. They believe that Putin’s actions led to Navalny’s death. Navalny became popular for showing corruption in Putin’s government, which gave hope to some Russians for changes in politics. Navalny’s sudden death leaves a significant gap in Russia’s opposition movement because he was its leading figure. Russian officials didn’t confirm the cause of Navalny’s death, but many people suspect that he didn’t die naturally. Difficult words: critic (a person who openly says negative things about someone or something), corruption (dishonest behavior of people in politics or other people in power), significant (important, big). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Alexei Navalny is a strong critic of Russian President Putin. Navalny goes to prison for many years. The prison is in the north of Russia. It is very cold there. Navalny fights against bad things in Russia. Many people believe in better times. Last week, Navalny dies. Leaders in the West say that Putin is responsible for Navalny’s death. Now, without Navalny, there is no other strong person. Nobody fights against the government. Navalny’s death makes many people sad. They want things to change. It is hard to speak out against strong people like Putin. Russian officials do not say why Navalny dies. Some people believe that Navally does not die naturally . Difficult words: critic (a person who openly says negative things about someone or something), responsible (to have control over something), naturally (in a normal way). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Residents of Hooke Close in Corby, Northamptonshire, UK, are outraged after an 18-meter-high warehouse was built behind their homes. The council mistakenly consulted residents of Hubble Road, causing confusion and frustration. The development, located on the site of a former Weetabix factory, has left residents feeling trapped and surrounded by noise and vibrations. Many fear the warehouse will block sunlight and lower property values. Despite apologies from the council, residents demand action, calling for the warehouse’s removal. The error highlights the importance of proper consultation in community planning projects to avoid such disruptions and conflicts in the future. Difficult words: outraged (extremely angry), consult (to have discussions with someone before taking action). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Residents of Hooke Close in Corby, Northamptonshire, UK, are angry. The council made a mistake and it approved the building of an 18-meter-high warehouse just behind their homes. The council spoke to residents of Hubble Road instead, which is a few hundred meters away. Workers are building the warehouse on the former Weetabix factory site, and it is causing noise and vibrations. It has an impact on residents’ daily lives. They worry about sunlight obstruction and property devaluation . The council apologized for its mistake, but the construction continues. Residents demand solutions, including the removal of the warehouse. Difficult words: warehouse (a large building for storing materials and products), obstruction (something what blocks a road, entrance, energy, and so on), devaluation (reducing the value of something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Not so long ago, Hooke Close in Corby, UK, is just a normal street. But now, people who live there are angry. Workers are building a warehouse behind their homes. How can it happen? The council makes a mistake. They speak to people who live in a different street. The warehouse is 18 meters high. People are upset about it. The warehouse is in a place where a factory is in the past. The construction makes noise. Houses are shaking. People cannot sleep. They worry about losing sunlight and the prices of their homes. The council says sorry. But it is not enough. People do not want the warehouse in their street. The construction continues. Difficult words: warehouse (a large building where people store materials and products), council (a group of people who deal with the affairs of a city or town), construction (building something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Indonesia’s presidential race, candidates are using TikTok to engage with young voters. Irene, a 22-year-old, uploads various content on TikTok, attracting attention from all three candidates. Prabowo, once a tough military figure, now showcases his softer side with quirky dance moves. His supporters even share videos of themselves crying for him. Other contenders, Anies and Ganjar, also increased their presence on the platform. Despite TikTok’s popularity among young voters, there are concerns about misinformation and manipulated content, including deepfake videos. Nevertheless, TikTok claims to combat harmful misinformation and prohibits political ads and fundraising. Experts emphasize the importance of candidates creating entertaining content to appeal to young voters. With millions of users, TikTok has become a significant battleground for Indonesian politicians seeking to sway the electorate. Difficult words: quirky (unusual or unpredictable), deepfake (a video in which a person’s face or body has been digitally altered so that they appear to be someone else), sway (to control or influence). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

During the Indonesian presidential campaign , candidates turned to TikTok to connect with young voters. Prabowo is one of the candidates. He was a tough and serious man who now shares funny videos, and he inspires others to do the same. Anies and Ganjar are also becoming more active on TikTok, and they communicate with voters. But some people worry that a lot of information on TikTok is fake. Young people may not know about Prabowo’s past problems. There are many fake images and videos on TikTok, but TikTok says that they fight with false information. TikTok bans political ads but it may not be enough. Experts say that these days candidates need to be funny to attract young voters because TikTok plays a key role in Indonesian politics. Difficult words: campaign (organized actions to achieve something), ad (an advertisement), attract (to make someone interested). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People in Indonesia are voting for a new president. Candidates must use TikTok. TikTok is very popular among young people. Candidates must be active on TikTok to reach young voters . Prabowo is once a tough man. But now, he shares funny videos. Anies and Ganjar also join TikTok. But false information is a problem on TikTok. There are many fake pictures and videos. Some voters do not know about Prabowo’s past. TikTok wants to solve the problem with fake information. But it is not easy. Experts say that fun videos are important. TikTok is important in the election . Difficult words: candidate (a person who takes part in the election), voter (a person who can or votes), election (a process where people choose leaders). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

NATO commences its largest military exercises in decades, named Operation Steadfast Defender, across Europe. Sweden, though not a NATO member, participates, aiming to boost resilience against potential threats. With fears of conflict with Russia looming , Swedish schools integrate war preparedness into their curriculum. One teacher, OA Lind, incorporates news programs to discuss emergency protocols with students. This approach helps allay anxiety and foster a sense of safety. However, not all children receive such support, and social media exacerbates fears, leading to increased calls to helplines. The Swedish government’s warnings, coupled with TikTok notifications, intensify concerns. Despite criticism, officials defend their actions, emphasizing the need for preparedness. NATO endorses Sweden’s measures as exemplary for all allies, advocating for citizen readiness in the face of potential disasters. Difficult words: loom (to seem about to happen), allay (to reduce), endorse (to declare approval or support), exemplary (serving as a desirable model). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

NATO begins its largest military exercises, Operation Steadfast Defender, across Europe. It includes Sweden, although Sweden is not a member of NATO. In response to possible conflict with Russia, Swedish schools explain to children how to be ready for war. OA Lind, a teacher, incorporates news programs and she discusses emergency plans with students. She hopes that it will make children less scared. But social media bring negative news, and more people call helplines . The government says that it is necessary to warn people so that they are ready in case a conflict starts. NATO sees Sweden as a model for other countries, saying that it is important to get ready for war in Europe. Difficult words: response (a reaction or answer), incorporate (to take in or include), helpline (a telephone service which provides advice and help). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hungarian President Katalin Novak resigned amid controversy over pardoning a man involved in covering up sexual abuse in a children’s home. Novak’s close ties to Prime Minister Viktor Orban intensified pressure for her resignation, sparking public outcry and opposition demands for accountability . Orban’s political setback comes as Hungary faces economic challenges and European Parliament elections. The scandal led to the resignation of former Justice Minister Judit Varga and prompted Orban to propose a constitutional amendment restricting the president’s pardoning power in cases of child-related crimes. Despite Fidesz’s leading position in polls, the scandal underscores political uncertainty ahead of the upcoming elections. Difficult words: outcry (a protest), accountability (responsibility), underscore (to emphasize). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The president of Hungary Katalin Novak resigned. She pardoned a man who was involved in a case of sexual abuse in a children’s home. Novak’s ties to Prime Minister Viktor Orban made people angry and there were protests. The opposition wanted Novak to resign. Prime Minister Viktor Orban tried to fix things by changing the rules, but it didn’t stop the scandal . Now, the head of the ruling party and another leader also resigned. Even though Orban’s party is leading now, people are unsure about the upcoming elections. Difficult words: pardon (to excuse or forgive), sexual abuse (making someone take part in sexual activities without their wish or agreement), scandal (an action or event which makes many people angry or upset). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Katalin Novak is the president of Hungary. She resigns . Novak lets a man leave prison. The man is part of hiding bad things that happen to children in a children’s home. People get angry when the man gets free. Some politicians want Novak to leave. The boss of the Hungarian government , Viktor Orban, tries to help. He changes some rules. But Novak leaves anyway. Now, the leader of the ruling party and another important person leave the government. Orban’s party is still popular. But people are not sure about the next vote. Poland, alongside Germany and the Netherlands, has signed the ‘military Schengen’ agreement, aiming to improve troop mobility among European states. The agreement is a response to security concerns heightened by Russia’s behavior, and it facilitates rapid aid for Ukraine and enhances NATO’s eastern flank readiness. Polish Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz emphasized the necessity of swift troop mobilization in light of the conflict in Ukraine. Dutch Ambassador Daphne Bergsma highlighted the significance of military mobility in addressing geopolitical challenges. For Poland, deeply involved in internal and external security issues, initiatives like military Schengen not only bolster security but also strengthen its EU standing following a change in government. Difficult words: facilitate (to make an action or process easier), mobilization (movement of troops), bolster (to support or strengthen). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Poland, Germany, and the Netherlands signed the ‘military Schengen’ agreement . The reason is moving soldiers faster in Europe. This comes as Russia’s actions worry Poland. The agreement helps Ukraine and improves NATO’s readiness to react to anything what Russia does. Poland’s Defense Minister says that being able to move soldiers quickly is very important because of the Ukraine conflict. The Dutch Ambassador thinks this is necessary for facing future problems. For Poland, this is important for both security and EU status after a change in government. Difficult words: agreement (a deal), readiness (being prepared for something), status (the situation at a particular time during a process). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Poland, Germany, and the Netherlands make a deal. They help each other move soldiers quickly in Europe. They do this because Russia worries Poland. The deal helps Ukraine and NATO. Poland says that moving soldiers fast is very important. It is because of the war in Ukraine. The Dutch Ambassador thinks this is very important for big challenges. Nobody knows what can happen in the future. The deal helps Poland. The country needs to be safe. It needs to be strong in the EU after a change in the government . Difficult words: soldier (a person who fights in a war), ambassador (an official who represents a country in another country), government (a group of people who lead a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

German media allege that a partner company of BASF, a chemical giant, is involved in human rights abuses in China’s Xinjiang region. The investigation revealed that employees of the partner company were reportedly spying on Uighur households, aiding the Chinese government’s re-education campaign. BASF has denied involvement in forced labor or human rights violations; however, critics find their defense questionable, given the shared compound and potential complicity of their joint ventures. Similar allegations have targeted other companies like Toyota and Volkswagen, indicating a systemic issue in China’s supply chains. Despite economic interests, companies must prioritize ethical production and consider divesting from Chinese supply chains to avoid supporting forced labor. While the EU’s proposed supply chain law is a step forward, experts argue it may not effectively address state-imposed forced labor in Xinjiang. Difficult words: compound (something formed by a union of elements or parts), complicity (involvement in wrongdoing), divest (to remove investments). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

German media accused a partner company of a chemical giant BASF of being involved in human rights violations in China’s Xinjiang region. According to the investigation, employees of this partner company spied on Uighur households in 2018. BASF denied this, but critics are not happy with their explanation. Similar allegations surfaced against big car manufacturers like Toyota and Volkswagen. To stop forced labor, companies might need to leave Chinese supply chains. But companies may have troubles with money because China is a big economy and it produces many parts. The EU is considering a new supply chain law which would deal with environmental and human rights, but it is not clear how effective it will be. Difficult words: violation (doing something what is not allowed by a law or rule), spy (to secretly get information about someone), allegation (claim). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Paris is aiming to make its city greener for the 2024 Olympics. They’ve decided to target SUV drivers by raising parking fees significantly. Despite low voter turnout , SUV drivers may face a threefold increase in parking charges, potentially paying 8 euros per hour and 225 euros for extended stays. Advocates argue that larger vehicles not only contribute more to pollution but also occupy excessive space, advocating for alternative modes of transportation like biking or using public transit. However, critics highlight the financial burden these places on families and the necessity of cars for certain activities. Despite the modest participation, Paris officials view the decision as a positive move towards environmental sustainability, urging car manufacturers to produce smaller, more eco-friendly vehicles. Difficult words: turnout (the number of people attending or taking part in an event), burden (hardship or distress). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Paris wants to make its city greener for the 2024 Olympics. They decided to make parking more expensive for SUVs . Only a few people voted on this change. SUVs might have to pay three times more for parking now. People who support this change say that big cars cause more pollution and use too much space. They think people should use bikes or trains instead. But others say that it is too expensive to stop using cars. Paris leaders are happy about the vote and they expect to take action. They even want car makers to make smaller cars. Difficult words: SUV (a large powerful car), pollution (making the air, water, or soil dirty). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Paris wants to make the city greener for the Olympics in 2024. They are making SUV parking more expensive. SUVs are large strong cars. They are very popular nowadays. Few people vote on this. SUVs may pay more for parking. People say that big cars pollute more. Also, they use too much space. People should use bikes or trains. But some people say that it is too expensive to stop using cars. Paris leaders consider this vote. They want car makers to make smaller cars. Difficult words: vote (to formally choose between two or more things, people, and so on), pollute (to make the air, water, or soil dirty), consider (to think something through). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Lewis Hamilton, the seven-time Formula 1 world champion, has announced his departure from Mercedes at the end of the 2024 season, signing a multi-year deal with Ferrari. Despite committing to Mercedes until 2025, Hamilton activated a release clause in his contract, citing the desire for a new challenge. His move to Ferrari signals a significant shift in F1 dynamics, with expectations high for his potential to lead Ferrari to their first driver’s title since 2007. Hamilton’s decision leaves Mercedes searching for a replacement driver, while Ferrari eagerly awaits his arrival, hoping to capitalize on his expertise in their pursuit of success. Difficult words: clause (a particular and separate article or section in a treaty or contract), capitalize (to profit from something), expertise (expert skill or knowledge in a particular field). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Seven-time Formula 1 champion Lewis Hamilton will depart from Mercedes at the end of 2024. He will join Ferrari on a multi-year deal. Hamilton recently extended his contract with Mercedes, but he invoked a release clause . He said that he wanted a fresh challenge with Ferrari. His move changes the F1, and many people hope for Ferrari’s first driver’s title since 2007. Mercedes must now find another driver. Ferrari hopes that Hamilton will be a good leader on their way to success. Difficult words: multi-year (lasting more than one year), invoke (to refer to), release clause (a person’s contract which speaks about transfer and money which a club must pay in such a situation). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Russian cosmonaut Oleg Kononenko recently broke the world record for the longest time spent in space, surpassing his compatriot Gennady Padalka. Kononenko achieved this milestone while aboard the International Space Station (ISS). He expressed his passion for space exploration, emphasizing his love for the work over setting records. Kononenko, who is orbiting approximately 423 miles from Earth, highlighted the physical challenges of space travel, including the effects of weightlessness. Despite technological advances allowing for better communication with loved ones back on Earth, he lamented missing out on significant moments with family during his extended missions. Kononenko’s journey reflects Russia’s enduring legacy in space exploration, despite challenges faced by its space program over the years. Difficult words: compatriot (a person from one’s own country), lament (to express sorrow or regret), legacy (the long-lasting effect of particular events or actions). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Russian cosmonaut Oleg Kononenko recently broke the record for the longest time spent in space, and he surpassed another Russian Gennady Padalka. Kononenko achieved this aboard the International Space Station (ISS). He spoke about the physical troubles during space travel and the impact which it had on his family life. Thanks to modern technologies, he could communicate with loved ones back on Earth, but he still regrets missing out on important moments with family during his extended missions. While Russia’s space program is facing difficulties, Kononenko is still committed to his job. Difficult words: surpass (to be faster, better, or bigger than something or somebody else), extended (long), committed (willing to give time and energy into something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
